newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch on alert for first case of mad cow disease.
newsitem.headline: Dutch on alert for first case of mad cow disease.

text.p: Dutch farm officials said on Wednesday they were combing farms in the country for what may be the Netherlands' first case of mad cow disease.

The hunt was launched after confirmation on Tuesday of the first cow born in Germany with the disease. Dutch farm officials said they had been informed by Germany that the mother of that cow was probably exported to the Netherlands in 1995.
"We are now trying to locate that cow; it is possible that she has had other calves since arriving here," a spokesman for the Dutch Agriculture Ministry told Reuters.
"But we can't say for sure the cow is here or if it has the disease."

The German cow, the country's fifth case of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) but the first born there to die of the disease, was calf to a Galloway cow imported from Britain. It was this animal, as part of a herd of 39 Galloways, that Germany believes was then exported to the Netherlands.
The German ministry said the cow, which was born in 1992, had not been infected by contaminated animal feed, leaving only the possibility it had contracted BSE from its mother.

Earlier on Wednesday, German farm minister Jochen Borchert said he supported the mass slaughter of all cattle originating from Britain. He said there were about 3,000 cattle in Germany imported from Britain and they had produced around 7,000 calves.
The Dutch farm ministry could give no firm comparable figures for the Netherlands but said they were expected to be lower than in Germany.
In April last year the Dutch began the slaughter of 64,000 imported British calves over fears of mad cow disease.
